title: Quadratic Function Word Problems
explanation: Identify variables and domains, optimize a model or solve a target equation, and report meaningful units.
WHAT YOU NEED TO KNOW / CORE IDEA
Quadratics model changing rates and turning points.
Area, revenue, profit, and height can follow f(x)=ax²+bx+c. Negative a gives a maximum; positive a gives a minimum.
A model represents a situation. Its domain contains allowed inputs. The vertex is the turning point; roots give output zero. Break-even means profit zero.
Use vertex for an optimum and roots for a target.
For f(x)=ax²+bx+c, vertex x=−b/(2a), y=f(−b/(2a)). For target T solve f(x)=T and check domain.
Define x and units; build the quadratic; identify the valid domain; choose vertex or target equation; solve and reject invalid roots.
If demand is 60−3p, R(p)=p(60−3p)=−3p²+60p. Vertex p=10 gives maximum revenue $300.
For 40 m of fence along three sides, A(x)=x(40−2x)=−2(x−10)²+200. The maximum area is 200 m².
For h(t)=−4t²+16t+2, the vertex is at t=2 seconds and h=18 meters.
Two quantities can meet one target.
R(q)=50q−2q² has vertex (12.5,312.5), zeros 0 and 25, and outputs R(10)=R(15)=300.
Reject negative time or length, keep units, distinguish vertex input from output, and distinguish revenue from profit.
Use −b/(2a) for extrema; factor or use the quadratic formula for target equations; verify by substitution.
R(q)=q(20−q) gives R(5)=75. For h(t)=−5t²+20t+1, h(1)=16. For C(x)=2(x−3)²+32, minimum is 32.
State the model and domain, solve for vertex or target, check roots, and give units.

practice.question: Profit P(x)=−(x−4)²+16 is in hundreds of dollars. State its maximum.
practice.solution: The square is minimized at x=4; P(4)=16 hundreds.

practice.question: Forty meters of fence cover three sides of a rectangle against a wall. The perpendicular sides are x m. Find maximum area.
A ball follows h(t)=−4t²+16t+2 meters. Find its maximum height and time.
At price p dollars, a store sells 60−3p items. Find price and maximum revenue.
A rectangle has width x m, length x+6 m, and area 72 m². Find its dimensions.
Profit P(x)=−(x−2)(x−10) for 0≤x≤12. Find break-even and positive-profit ranges.
practice.solution: Roots are 2 and 10; the negative product is positive between roots.

practice.question: Height h(t)=−5t²+25t meters. Find the positive time when the ball lands.
practice.solution: −5t(t−5)=0, so t=0 or 5; t=5 is landing.

practice.question: Revenue R(p)=p(100−4p), 0≤p≤25. Find the maximizing price and revenue.
Cost C(x)=2x²−12x+50 dollars. Find minimum cost.
Height h(t)=−5t²+30t+10 meters. When does it return to launch height 10 m?
practice.solution: Set h=10: −5t(t−6)=0; take the later root.

practice.question: Demand p=50−2q. Find quantities 0≤q≤25 that yield $300 revenue.
A rectangle has perimeter 60 m and area 200 m². Find side lengths.
Profit P(x)=−2x²+24x−40 dollars. Find maximum profit.
Height h(t)=−5t²+20t+15 meters. Find positive ground-hit time exactly and to two decimals.
practice.solution: Set h=0: t²−4t−3=0, so t=2±√7. Reject negative time.

practice.question: Profit P(x)=−(x−8)²+64 dollars. Find all x≥0 for which profit is at least $48.
Profit P(x)=−3x²+48x−60 dollars. Find its maximum and exact break-even levels.

test.question: For A(x)=x(20−x), what is the maximum area?
For R(q)=40q−q², which quantities give revenue 300?
For P(x)=−2x²+16x−18, what is maximum profit?
For h(t)=−5t²+20t+5, at which times is h=20?

desmos.lookFor: Vertex (12.5,312.5), zeros 0 and 25, and y=300 intersections x=10 and 15.
desmos.useIt: Check maximum revenue and quantities producing $300 within 0≤x≤25.
desmos.why: The downward parabola has its maximum at the vertex; horizontal intersections solve target revenue.
desmos.faster: Exact vertex algebra and factoring are faster; Desmos verifies graph interpretation.

english: Quadratic word problems model area, revenue, profit, and height. Define your variables and units.
Real-world inputs may be restricted to nonnegative time, positive length, or feasible sales.
The vertex input is −b/(2a). A negative leading coefficient gives a maximum.
With 40 meters of fencing for three sides, A(x)=x(40−2x)=−2(x−10)²+200.
For h(t)=−4t²+16t+2, maximum height is 18 meters after 2 seconds.
To find revenue 300, set R(q)=300, not just the vertex.
For R(q)=50q−2q², quantities 10 and 15 both give $300.
The revenue vertex is (12.5,312.5); roots are 0 and 25. Algebra confirms the graph.
Choose vertex or equation, respect domain, check by substitution, and state units.
arabic: مقدمة
المسائل الكلامية التربيعية تمثل المساحة والإيراد والربح والارتفاع. حدد المتغيرات ووحداتها.
المجال
الزمن غير سالب والطول موجب والكمية المباعة ضمن حدود الطلب.
قاعدة الرأس
إحداثي الرأس الأفقي هو −b/(2a). المعامل السالب لـ x² يعني قيمة عظمى.
الإيراد
R(p)=p(60−3p)=−3p²+60p؛ السعر الأمثل 10 دولارات والإيراد 300 دولار.
المساحة
باستخدام 40 متراً من السياج لثلاثة أضلاع: A(x)=x(40−2x)=−2(x−10)²+200.
الارتفاع
في h(t)=−4t²+16t+2 تكون القمة 18 متراً بعد ثانيتين.
القيمة المطلوبة
لإيجاد كمية تحقق إيراد 300 نحل R(q)=300، وليس فقط الرأس.
جذران
في R(q)=50q−2q² تحقق الكميتان 10 و15 إيراد 300 دولار.
الرسم وديسموس
رأس منحنى الإيراد (12.5,312.5) وجذراه صفر و25. الجبر يؤكد الرسم.
الخلاصة
اختر الرأس أو المعادلة، واحترم المجال، وتحقق بالتعويض، واكتب الوحدات.
